specAnchors.text: be able to define the terms ‘enthalpy change of solution, ∆ sol H ’ and ‘ enthalpy change of hydration , ∆ hyd H of an ion’

primer.text: Dissolving an ionic solid has two energetic faces: the endothermic breakdown of the lattice and the exothermic hydration of its ions. This note defines the enthalpy of solution and the enthalpy of hydration, writes their equations with state symbols, and shows how polar water molecules bind ions through ion-dipole attractions.

modules.title: Solution and hydration enthalpies
modules.opening: Two definitions run the whole solution-energetics topic. The enthalpy of solution covers one mole of solid dissolving into infinitely dilute solution - exothermic or endothermic, compound by compound. The enthalpy of hydration covers one mole of gaseous ions entering water - always exothermic, because ion-dipole attractions form as polar water molecules wrap the ions.
keyPoints: The standard enthalpy change of solution (delta sol H): the enthalpy change that results when enough water dissolves 1 mole of an ionic substance to make an infinitely dilute solution.
The (aq) symbol records dissolution in sufficient water; for potassium chloride: KCl (s) plus aq forming KCl (aq), or as separated ions K+ (aq) and Cl- (aq).
Delta sol H can be exothermic (negative) or endothermic (positive), depending on the compound.

The standard enthalpy change of hydration (delta hyd H): the enthalpy change that results when 1 mole of a stated gaseous ion enters water to give an infinitely dilute solution, as in Mg2+ (g) plus aq forming Mg2+ (aq).
Hydration enthalpies are exothermic: energy is released as attractions form between the ions and water molecules.
Water is polar, with a delta-negative oxygen and delta-positive hydrogens, so ion-dipole attractions form: oxygen faces positive ions and hydrogens face negative ions.

low.restatement: Solution enthalpy: solid plus aq, either sign. Hydration enthalpy: gaseous ion plus aq, always negative, thanks to ion-dipole attractions.
low.analogy: Moving house (dissolving) versus settling into a furnished flat (hydrating): the first may cost or gain, the second always furnishes warmth.
low.examPointer: Write the state symbols aq and g exactly - definitions are graded on them.

medium.restatement: Dissolution has two faces - break the lattice, then let water embrace each ion - and hydration is the embracing term, always releasing energy because new attractions form.
medium.analogy: Undoing a packing crate (lattice) and then arranging each item on a shelf that fits it (hydration).
medium.examPointer: The 'infinitely dilute' phrase guards against ion-ion interactions - quote it in definitions.

glossary.definition: The enthalpy change when 1 mole of ionic substance dissolves in enough water to make an infinitely dilute solution.
The enthalpy change when 1 mole of gaseous ion dissolves in water to form an infinitely dilute solution; always exothermic.
The attraction between an ion and the delta charges of polar water molecules.
